newsitem.title: USA: Anxiety and depression can predict hypertension.
newsitem.headline: Anxiety and depression can predict hypertension.

text.p: People who suffer from anxiety and depression are more than twice as likely to develop high blood pressure, U.S. federal scientists reported on Tuesday.
High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, can lead to fatal heart problems or strokes.

Researchers from the National Centre for Health Statistics, a branch of the Centres for Disease Control, said that their finding applied to blacks and whites, but the risk of high blood pressure was higher for blacks.

Lead researcher Bruce Jonas and colleagues studied 3,000 men and women from age 24 to 64. They had no high blood pressure at the start of the study, but as he tracked them for seven to 16 years, he found a pattern.

Even intermediate levels of anxiety and depression were associated with a 60 percent greater likelihood of developing hypertension. That was true even when other factors, such as education, smoking, alcohol use, body mass, were taken into account.
The findings appear in the January/February edition of the Archives of Family Medicine.
